bib.title: PromptSource: An Integrated Development Environment and Repository for Natural Language Prompts
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the ACL, System Demonstrations, pages 93-104

read.skipped: Reference list tail skimmed only; appendix figures 6-9 are images with captions only.

question: How can users create, refine, share and reuse natural language prompts for datasets in a collaborative, quality-controlled way?
contributions: A templating language (Jinja2) for defining data-linked prompts
A web interface to iterate on prompts by viewing outputs on many examples
Community guidelines for contributing prompts to a common pool (P3)

method.summary: PromptSource is a Streamlit GUI plus Jinja2 template format integrated with HuggingFace Datasets. Prompts are functions mapping a dataset example to an input/target pair, written, documented, reviewed by code review, and merged into the Public Pool of Prompts (P3).
method.task: prompt authoring and repository for zero-shot / multitask prompted training

datasets.name: P3 (Public Pool of Prompts)
datasets.source: HuggingFace Datasets library datasets; prompts written by BigScience contributors

inference.prompting: Zero-shot, explicit task instructions, no priming examples; valid completions may be scored and the highest returned

eval.protocol: No experiments reported; prompts pass automatic tests and code review by other contributors.

results.claim: The PromptSource collection holds over 2,000 prompts for roughly 170 datasets.
results.setup: Public Pool of Prompts as of January 2022, all reviewed against the quality standards
results.quote: Over 2,000 prompts for roughly 170 datasets are already available in PromptSource.

results.claim: Authors were encouraged to write 5 to 10 or more prompts per dataset, varying formulation.
results.setup: Community guideline; Fig 6 shows most datasets have 5 to 10 prompts
results.quote: we encouraged prompt authors to create between 5 and 10 (or more)

results.claim: In early experiments, prompts that did not state the valid completions tended to perform worse than those that listed them; no numbers, models or datasets are given.

limits: No experiments or user study: design claims rest on authors' experience with a pilot prompt-writing effort.
Targets zero-shot and gradient-based few-shot; priming is not natively supported.
Prompt quality has no simple metric like inter-annotator agreement; quality is enforced by code review.
English prompts only in P3; other languages via translation in follow-on work.
